files.content:
1: package llmverify
2: 
3: import chisel3._
4: import chisel3.util._
5: import chiselFv._
6: 
7: // Model of a puzzle played on a square board with five rows of five holes.
8: // Initially, pegs are placed in 23 holes, leaving the hole in the center
9: // and the one in the lower right corner empty.
10: // Each move consist in removing one peg by jumping over it with another peg.
11: // A valid move required the jumping peg to be adjacent to the one to be
12: // removed and the hole on the other side to be empty.
13: // The objective is to remove all pegs except one.
14: 
15: class field5 extends Module with Formal {
16:   val io = IO(new Bundle {
17:     val from = Input(UInt(5.W))
18:     val dir = Input(UInt(2.W))
19:     val cnt = Output(UInt(5.W))
20:     // Add board output to preserve the design
21:     val board = Output(Vec(25, UInt(1.W)))
22:   })
23: 
24:   // Direction constants
25:   val U = 0.U(2.W)
26:   val D = 1.U(2.W)
27:   val L = 2.U(2.W)
28:   val R = 3.U(2.W)
29: 
30:   // Board representation as a vector of 25 bits
31:   val board = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(25)(1.U(1.W))))
32:   
33:   // Initialize board: center (12) and lower right corner (24) are empty
34:   board(12) := 0.U
35:   board(24) := 0.U
36: 
37:   // Compute the residue of a 5-bit number mod 5
38:   def resMod5(n: UInt): UInt = {
39:     val result = Wire(UInt(3.W))
40:     // Default assignment
41:     result := 4.U
42:     
43:     switch(n) {
44:       is(0.U, 5.U, 10.U, 15.U, 20.U, 25.U, 30.U) { result := 0.U }
45:       is(1.U, 6.U, 11.U, 16.U, 21.U, 26.U, 31.U) { result := 1.U }
46:       is(2.U, 7.U, 12.U, 17.U, 22.U, 27.U) { result := 2.U }
47:       is(3.U, 8.U, 13.U, 18.U, 23.U, 28.U) { result := 3.U }
48:     }
49:     result
50:   }
51: 
52:   // Move execution logic
53:   val nextBoard = Wire(Vec(25, UInt(1.W)))
54:   nextBoard := board
55: 
56:   // Define move conditions for verification
57:   val moveL = Wire(Bool())
58:   val moveR = Wire(Bool())
59:   val moveU = Wire(Bool())
60:   val moveD = Wire(Bool())
61:   moveL := false.B
62:   moveR := false.B
63:   moveU := false.B
64:   moveD := false.B
65: 
66:   when(io.from < 25.U && board(io.from) === 1.U) {
67:     switch(io.dir) {
68:       is(L) {
69:         when(resMod5(io.from) > 1.U) {
70:           when(board(io.from - 1.U) === 1.U && board(io.from - 2.U) === 0.U) {
71:             nextBoard(io.from) := 0.U
72:             nextBoard(io.from - 1.U) := 0.U
73:             nextBoard(io.from - 2.U) := 1.U
74:             moveL := true.B
75:           }
76:         }
77:       }
78:       is(R) {
79:         when(resMod5(io.from) < 3.U) {
80:           when(board(io.from + 1.U) === 1.U && board(io.from + 2.U) === 0.U) {
81:             nextBoard(io.from) := 0.U
82:             nextBoard(io.from + 1.U) := 0.U
83:             nextBoard(io.from + 2.U) := 1.U
84:             moveR := true.B
85:           }
86:         }
87:       }
88:       is(U) {
89:         when(io.from < 15.U) {
90:           when(board(io.from + 5.U) === 1.U && board(io.from + 10.U) === 0.U) {
91:             nextBoard(io.from) := 0.U
92:             nextBoard(io.from + 5.U) := 0.U
93:             nextBoard(io.from + 10.U) := 1.U
94:             moveU := true.B
95:           }
96:         }
97:       }
98:       is(D) {
99:         when(io.from > 9.U) {
100:           when(board(io.from - 5.U) === 1.U && board(io.from - 10.U) === 0.U) {
101:             nextBoard(io.from) := 0.U
102:             nextBoard(io.from - 5.U) := 0.U
103:             nextBoard(io.from - 10.U) := 1.U
104:             moveD := true.B
105:           }
106:         }
107:       }
108:     }
109:   }
110: 
111:   val moveExecuted = (io.from < 25.U && board(io.from) === 1.U) && (moveL || moveR || moveU || moveD)
112: 
113:   // Update board on clock edge
114:   board := nextBoard
115: 
116:   // Count the number of pegs on the board
117:   io.cnt := board.map(x => x).reduce(_ + _)
118:   
119:   // Output board state for verification
120:   io.board := board
121: 
122:   // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
123:   // Formal Verification Assertions
124:   // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
125: 
126:   // --- Registers for tracking history ---
127:   val prevCnt = RegNext(io.cnt)                                        // Peg count from previous cycle
128:   val initDone = RegInit(false.B)                                      // False only in the first cycle after reset
129:   initDone := true.B
130:   val firstCycle = RegInit(true.B)                                     // True only in the first cycle after reset
131:   firstCycle := false.B
132:   val moveDelayed = RegNext(moveExecuted)                              // Move signal delayed by one cycle
133: 
134:   // --- Count how many board positions change between current and next state ---
135:   val changedPositions = (0 until 25).map(i => board(i) =/= nextBoard(i)).map(b => b.asUInt).reduce(_ + _)
136: 
137:   // ==========================================================================
138:   // Safety: Peg count must never increase from one cycle to the next.
139:   // In peg solitaire, each valid move removes exactly one peg, so the count
140:   // is monotonically non-increasing. An increase would indicate a logic error.
141:   // ==========================================================================
142:   fvAssert(!initDone || prevCnt >= io.cnt, "cnt_non_increasing")
143: 
144:   // ==========================================================================
145:   // Correctness: After reset, the board must have exactly 23 pegs.
146:   // The design initializes all 25 positions to 1, then sets positions 12 and
147:   // 24 to 0, yielding a count of 23.
148:   // ==========================================================================
149:   fvAssert(!firstCycle || io.cnt === 23.U, "initial_cnt_23")
150: 
151:   // ==========================================================================
152:   // Correctness: Each valid move decreases the peg count by exactly 1.
153:   // When a move executes: source peg (1→0), jumped peg (1→0), destination (0→1).
154:   // Total change: -1 peg. If the count decreases by a different amount, the
155:   // move logic has a bug (e.g. updating the wrong positions).
156:   // ==========================================================================
157:   fvAssert(!moveDelayed || io.cnt === prevCnt - 1.U, "cnt_decrease_by_one_on_move")
158: 
159:   // ==========================================================================
160:   // Consistency: Exactly 3 board positions change when a move executes; no
161:   // positions change when no move executes. This verifies that the move logic
162:   // updates exactly the three intended positions (source, jumped, destination)
163:   // and no others, and that no spurious updates occur without a move.
164:   // ==========================================================================
165:   fvAssert(!moveExecuted || changedPositions === 3.U, "three_positions_change_on_move")
166:   fvAssert(moveExecuted || changedPositions === 0.U, "no_change_without_move")
167: 
168:   // ==========================================================================
169:   // Encoding: At most one direction can be active at any time.
170:   // The switch statement enforces mutual exclusion, but this assertion guards
171:   // against simulation-rare glitches or encoding bugs that could corrupt io.dir.
172:   // ==========================================================================
173:   assertMutex(Seq(io.dir === U, io.dir === D, io.dir === L, io.dir === R), "dir_mutex")
174: }
175: 
176: object VerilogGenerator extends App {
177:   emitVerilog(new field5(), args)
178: }
